signed_predicate: For each in-scope instance, FAIL if any associated public IPv4/IPv6 address or internet-facing load balancer target has a route and security-group path to a listening port; UNKNOWN on incomplete route, target or ingress inventory.
catalog_title: EC2 instances should not have a public IP address

decision.reason: The exact signed predicate requires a public path to a listening port and the historical handler requires ListeningPortVerified plus complete listener/target/route/ingress inventories. The available independently validated native model proves only a bounded direct IPv4 configuration allowance, with application_listening=unknown and all_paths_evaluated=false. Neither that positive witness nor its absence settles the old listener contract. PublicReachability assertions in legacy fixtures have no authoritative listener producer. Quarantine this exact historical contract while preserving lineage and keeping the active native configuration alternatives available. This is an unsupported evidence/semantics classification, not an owner-input requirement or a blanket claim that future AWS-native ELB/telemetry proofs are impossible.
decision.future_boundary: A separately specified provider-managed ELB listener and healthy-target proof could merit investigation; this model excludes ELB paths and equivalence to the historical listener predicate was not established.
